parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes to create a new Border Security Command with counter-terrorism style powers to tackle criminal gangs behind small boat crossings, clear the asylum backlog through additional caseworkers, establish a returns enforcement unit, and reduce net migration by reforming the points-based immigration system and linking immigration with skills policy.

citations.quote: We will create a new Border Security Command, with hundreds of new investigators, intelligence officers, and cross-border police officers.
Labour will reduce net migration. We will reform the points-based immigration system so that it is fair and properly managed, with and by linking immigration and skills policy.

results.headline: Labour pledges swift, firm and fair asylum system
results.quote: Labour will restore order to the asylum system so that it operates swiftly, firmly, and fairly; and the rules are properly enforced.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives propose a legally binding annual cap on migration that falls each year, with a parliamentary vote on the level, and commit to a continual programme of removing illegal migrants to Rwanda with regular monthly flights until small boat crossings stop, while raising salary thresholds for skilled worker and family visas.

citations.quote: We will introduce a binding, legal cap on migration, set on work and family visas so public services are protected whilst we bring the skills our businesses and the NHS needs.
We will run a relentless, continual process of permanently removing illegal migrants to Rwanda with a regular rhythm of flights every month, starting this July, until the boats are stopped.

results.headline: Conservatives pledge legal migration cap to guarantee falling numbers
results.quote: Introduce a legal cap on migration to guarantee that numbers will fall every year, so public services are protected while bringing in the skills we need.

results.headline: Conservative MP credits ETA scheme as Conservative border reform
results.quote: The ETA scheme was introduced by the Conservative Government to secure and modernise Britain's borders.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose scrapping the Rwanda scheme and the Illegal Migration Act, ending the Hostile Environment, replacing the salary threshold for work visas with a flexible merit-based system, and providing safe and legal routes for refugees including new humanitarian travel permits and a scheme to resettle unaccompanied child refugees.

citations.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees, helping to prevent dangerous Channel crossings.
Creating new humanitarian travel permits that would allow asylum seekers to travel to the UK safely to proceed with their claims.

results.headline: Lib Dems pledge to scrap Rwanda scheme and uphold Refugee Convention
results.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees.
